parole.testo: Borrowed from a Northwestern Iranian or Central Iranian term descending from Proto-Iranian *hapáθniH (“co-wife”).
Borrowed from Northwestern Iranian, from Proto-Iranian [Term?].

Borrowed from a Northwestern Iranian cognate of Manichaean Middle Persian 𐫤𐫗𐫉- (tnz- /⁠tanz-⁠/, “to strain, press”), from Proto-Iranian *tanč- (“to twist (together), become narrow, dense, constrict”), from Proto-Indo-European *tenk- (“to compact”). Akin to Ossetian тындзын (tynʒyn), Old Armenian տան

parole.significato: cockroach; ellipsis of سوسک حمام (susk-e hammâm)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Northwestern Iranian, cf. Larestani لاس (lâs, “female dog”), Gilaki لاس (lâs, “female dog”), Bakhtiari لاس (lâs, “female dog”).
Northwestern Iranian variant of لب (lab, “lip”), see it.

Probably a loanword from Northwestern Iranian. Compare Gazi مکامن (mekāmun, “to suck”). Ultimately from Proto-Iranian *maič- (“to suck”), Northern Luri مژنیێ (mejnyı, “to suck”), which has no clear Indo-European etymology. Doublet of مزیدن (mazīdan, “to taste”), which was inherited from Middle Persi

parole.significato: making a hole, digging out, making hollow; excavation; a mine, a trench
parole.testo: Probably a Northwestern Iranian borrowing, also found in Azerbaijani nəğım, nəğm, Middle Armenian նաղմ (naġm), Central Kurdish نەغم (neẍim, “tunnel”), Ottoman Turkish لغم (lağım), Arabic لَغْم (laḡm), لَغَم (laḡam), لُغْم (luḡm, “mine, tunnel”), and again Persian نغن (naġan, “navel-hole”). A Northwestern Iranian doublet of آلو (âlu, “plum”), compare Mazanderani هلی (halī, “plum”), Northern Kurdish hilîk, hilûk, halûk, helûje, hulîk, hulûk, helû, hulû etc., Central Kurdish هەڵووچە (hellûçe), هەڵووژە (hellûje, “plum”).
Borrowed from a Northwestern Iranian cognate of Persian خوش (xwaš) and thus a doublet of خوش (xwaš); see it for more.

Borrowed from Northwestern Iranian, whence borrowing Sanskrit जडुवार (jaḍuvāra), जडुपार (jaḍupāra), जदुवार (jaduvāra), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *gʷet- (“resin, gum”), also found as ژد (žad, “resin, gum”), as well as ـوار (-vâr, suffix denoting something having a characteristic).

Superficially a Northwestern Iranian formation in homage to the headwear’s jags from a stem “stinging, cutting” discussed for Persian گزنه (gazane, “nettle”), Gilaki گرزنه (garzane, “nettle”) and Classical Persian گرزه (garza, “rat”), because Jewish Literary Aramaic גרזנא (*garzənā), Hebrew גַּרְזֶן

Cognate with Bakhtiari گێز (gız, “mad”), Northern Luri گێژ (gıj, “mad”), Dezfuli گیز (geyz, “dizzy; confused”), Northern Kurdish gêj (“dizzy”), Sogdian [script needed] (kyc /⁠kēč⁠/).
